title: Jury Readback V1 (what GET /api/projects/<id>/jury answers)
$comment: Written against two payloads the product really emitted on 2026-10-08 -- one project holding an APPROVE verdict plus an agent proposal, and one project with nothing filed -- captured through design_lab.http_service.make_server on a live socket; see design-lab/scripts/verify_route_payload_contracts.py. Emitter: src/design_lab/jury_review.py (JuryReview.list). THE RECORDS ARE REFERENCED, NOT RESTATED: each element of `records` and each value of `current_verdicts` is the jury document itself, bound by design-lab/schemas/assurance-jury-record-v2.schema.json (a verdict matches the root, a proposal matches $defs/proposal). Copying those fields into this file would create a second authority able to disagree with the contract the write path already enforces, so a v2 change moves here by reference. `human_acceptance` is a sentence about the PROJECT: ACCEPTED requires at least one ACTIVE reviewable version and a current APPROVE for every one of them, which is why accepted_versions and reviewable_active_versions travel with it rather than being inferred from verdict_count.

allOf.$comment: An empty reviewable set is NOT_ACCEPTED on purpose: 'all zero of zero passed' is vacuously true and would read as a human gate nobody went through.

version_no.description: The revision number of the version on offer. reviewable_versions returns one row per asset -- the highest ACTIVE version_no it has -- so a reviewer cannot sign a superseded draft and have it count as acceptance.
